# Brass AI Axioms

> Brass AI Axioms is four free tools that find the point the code stops doing what you asked.

An AI coding agent reports that it is done. The code is almost right, so it ships.
It fails later. Brass AI Axioms checks the agent's output against the request that
produced it, and shows the exact point where the two stop matching.

Works with Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, and any LLM-driven coding agent.
No install. Free and open source.

## The four tools

- [The Axioms](https://github.com/hartforddavis-ai/brass-ai-axioms): Live. A 30-line rules file for CLAUDE.md/.cursorrules/AGENTS.md — makes the agent prove a change works before calling itself done, stops over-building, makes it own up to what broke. One paste, no install.
- [Blacksmith](https://github.com/hartforddavis-ai/blacksmith): Live. Runs your build step-by-step against the original spec, so drift shows at step 3 instead of buried in 40 files of changes. Runs locally, zero dependencies.
- VibeValve: Coming soon. Makes the agent re-check its own bug fix against what you asked for, clause by clause, before you hit merge.
- Gauge: Coming soon. Fact-checks every claim the agent makes about its own output — unverifiable claims don't pass.

## Facts

- Name: Brass AI Axioms, method also called "The Shearpin Process"
- Category: developer tool, AI code verification, AI coding agent guardrails
- Price: free
- Licence: open source
- Install: none required
- Publisher: Crucible Labs, Wapengo NSW, Australia
- Contact: thecruciblelabs@gmail.com

## Why the name

A shear pin is the part in a machine calibrated to give first, in one known place,
so the machinery downstream comes through clean — the image behind the method,
the Shearpin Process. Each tool sits at the joint where an unproven claim would
otherwise reach your code.
